correctness.rationale: Assessed the corrected /workspace/repairs/3/RESULT.md. The frozen line 48 infers that f_a*f_b is C² merely from an integrable second weak derivative of f_b; when f_a is only L¹ that does not establish continuity or pointwise evaluation at overlapping singular endpoints. The replacement supplies the missing estimates: for 0<a<1 and b>2, choose conjugate finite P,Q with 1/P>1−a and 1/Q>max(0,3−b), possible exactly under the sufficient total-rate condition a+b>3 in the singular b<3 subcase. Hölder and continuity of translations in L^Q give continuous derivatives through order two. For both rates above one, the second derivative is f_a' * f_b' and the analogous endpoint exponents max(0,2−a), max(0,2−b) sum to less than one. At a=1, b>2 makes f_b continuously differentiable through its support endpoints and gives p''(0)=0. The stationary center calculation cancels the interaction exactly; the single filter's two stationary orientation fluxes vanish at the endpoints, giving the normalized beta law with no boundary atoms. The half-sum has density 2(f_a*f_b)(2z), so its curvature is 8 times the centered differentiated convolution. Pairing the two terms and using B(3/2,s−3)=B(1/2,s−2)/(2(s−3)) gives the claimed positive coefficient for the mixed sector. Positivity, the strict central minimum and zero edge values force an interior maximum on each side by compactness. For a,b>1 the odd-derivative pairing yields a strictly negative integral at every positive interior argument; the uniform case has an explicit strictly negative derivative. Substitution x=1−2εt on the convolution interval gives factors 4εt and 4ε(1−t) at leading order and an integrable beta weight, proving the endpoint coefficient independently for every positive a,b. This also settles the equal-rate comparison directly: a=b=2 gives coefficient 6 and exponent 3. Only RESULT.md is corrected; the independent argument establishes the continuum theorem, not the frozen finite output.
